title: afl common skill
description: A skill written once and given to the agents of any step with "skills": ["<id>"]. Claude agents load it as a session plugin skill (afl-skills:<id>); other agents get its instructions in the prompt. Lives in workflows/skills (built-in), ~/.afl/skills or <repo>/.afl/skills.

$schema.description: This schema, for editors. afl ignores it.

id.description: Used in "skills" and as the file name; overrides a built-in or global skill with the same id.

description.description: What the skill does and when to use it; agents read this to decide when it applies.

tags.description: Tags to filter the library by in the UI and with --tag, e.g. review or planning: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

content.description: The instructions, in markdown: the body of the skill's SKILL.md.

files.description: Supporting text files the instructions refer to, by path relative to the skill's folder (not SKILL.md).

recommend.description: What kind of repo the skill suits, so runs there are offered it (afl skill recommend). It is recommended when one of its files matches a file in the repo, or when the repo's stack has one of its frameworks (or, for a skill naming no frameworks, one of its languages). Leave it out for a general skill that workflows pick themselves (1.2).

glob.description: A file pattern (* and ?), matched against each file's name, or against its path from the repo root when it has a /, e.g. *.csproj or src/*.py.

contains.description: Text the file must contain, ignoring case, e.g. fastapi in pyproject.toml. Only files up to 256 KB are read.

files.description: Files that show the skill fits; any one is enough.

languages.description: The languages the skill is for, e.g. csharp or python; offered when asking what an empty repo will use.

frameworks.description: The frameworks the skill is for, e.g. fastapi or playwright; offered when asking what an empty repo will use.

reason.description: The reason shown with the recommendation, e.g. C# project.
